definition: The contributor joins the program without a contract, at the manager's initiative.
Address printed on the invoice.
Held by the contributor's Organization, not entered per subscription.
The invoice keeps a copy of it when it is issued.
Files attached to the contract (example: house rules), each with a display name.
PDF only
An amendment is a change to the subscription that requires a signature. The amendment is the document the parties sign.
The contract generated by each new version of a subscription after the first one, within the same subscription group.
A contribution with a negative amount that corrects all or part of a contribution that is already due (refund, discount, mistake).
It can be linked to the contribution it corrects: it can then only be invoiced once that contribution has been invoiced. Without an original contribution, it can be invoiced directly.
Entered by hand; never invoiced automatically.
A workspace on the platform.
A single Cascade can own subscription models and/or contribute to those of others.
It always belongs to an Organization, which owns its legal identity.
The Organization's payment account with Stripe, connected from the Cascade settings; only one per organization, valid for all its Cascades, never replaced.
Required to collect contributions by SEPA direct debit.
States: missing address, not connected, incomplete registration, payments disabled, operational, access revoked.
List of the people (name and email) who sign contracts on behalf of the owning Cascade; at least one.
The first signer is the one whose name appears on the documents.
Membership method option: the contributor must sign a contract electronically, after uploading the supporting documents.
The contract is signed by the signer contacts of the owning Cascade and by the contributor.
The first version of a subscription group produces an initial contract; any change after signature goes through an amendment.
The contract number is built on the Cascade's prefix.
The contact designated in the subscription group to represent the contributor.
Has no account: they act only through signed links received by email (signature, document upload).
An amount owed by a contributor on a given date, generated by their subscription.
Generated automatically or added manually.
For recurring subscriptions, the contributions at the start and end of the period are prorated.
Statuses: new, pending, paid, partially paid, overdue.
How often a contribution is created.
Periods follow the calendar: weeks run from Monday to Sunday; months, quarters and years are calendar ones.
Date on which the subscription ends: no more contributions are created after it.
Pre-filled with the model's default end date.
Required for a one-time model, optional otherwise.
End date suggested when each subscription is created, which can be changed subscription by subscription.
Optional: if empty, contributions continue without limit.
Date from which the subscription (or its new version) is in force.
Common to all recurrence options.
The invoice is issued automatically this many days before the contribution date.
Empty: the manager issues invoices by hand.
Due date printed on the invoice, after which it is considered unpaid.
values: Immediately, 30 days end of month, 60 days end of month

definition: Number of days before the contribution date on which the SEPA direct debit takes place.
Required as soon as the model or one of its subscriptions uses SEPA direct debit.
Requires automatic invoicing, and at least 2 days between the invoice and the direct debit.
Label of the invoice line (example: "Monthly fee").
On the model: the list of documents the contributor must upload before signing the contract (example: home insurance, tax certificate).
On the subscription: the documents actually uploaded, one for each document requested.
Each one goes through the statuses pending → approved or rejected (approval by the manager).
Sending method option: the contributor receives an invoice by email for each contribution (example: fee charged to a company).
The invoice is generated from a contribution and numbered with the Cascade's prefix.
It freezes the billing data when it is issued, produces a PDF and is sent to the contributor by email.
A user who is a member of the Organization of an owning Cascade.
Manages the models, subscriptions and contributions from the application.
The model's identity: its name and its VAT rate.
Personal message included in the invitation email sent to the contributor.
How a contributor joins the program: by signing a contract or by simple membership.
How the contribution is claimed from the contributor: by invoice or by email.
Text of the amendments: a header, a footer and paragraphs.
Each paragraph has triggers: it appears in the amendment only if one of these fields has changed.
Formatted text of the contract, containing placeholders in [square brackets] that are replaced for each subscription.
The template of a program, defined by an owning Cascade; each subscription is based on a model.

It is configured in sections: General information (name, VAT rate), Recurrence (recurring, one-time or permanent, and recurrence cycle), Contribution amount, Sending method (invoice or email), Payment method, Contribution receipt, Membership method (contract or simple membership).
With contract membership, it also carries the contract template and the amendment template.
Who decides the amount of the contributions and how it changes.
The manager sets the amount of each subscription in advance.
Amount of a full contribution, excluding tax.
VAT and the amount incl. VAT are calculated from the model's rate.
How the contributor pays their contributions: payment method and, for direct debit, the direct debit lead time.
The model's default payment method, which can be changed on each subscription.
values: Bank card, SEPA transfer, SEPA direct debit, Cash, Cheque

definition: VAT number printed on the invoice, optional.
Held by the contributor's Organization.
The invoice keeps a copy of it when it is issued.
The legal entity (company name, company registration number, VAT, IBAN, billing address, logo), above the Cascade.
Groups one or more Cascades and holds the users' membership.
The payment (full or partial) of a contribution.
What the contributor has paid.
Only one contribution is created, but the subscription stays active indefinitely (example: lifetime membership fee, participating securities).
Each subscription generates only one contribution (example: room rental).
The end date is required on the subscription.
A one-time subscription cannot be changed (no amendment).
Short code of a Cascade (e.g. ACME), unique within the Organization and derived from the name if left blank.
Used to number contracts and invoices.
The document given to the contributor once the contribution is paid: simple receipt or tax receipt.
How contributions repeat over time: recurring, one-time or permanent.
A contribution is created for each period (example: monthly fee).
The contributions at the start and end of the period are prorated.
A contributor can subscribe to the same model several times.
The contact (name + email) designated in a subscription model to sign contracts on behalf of the owning Cascade.
Not necessarily a user.
A version within a subscription group (a contributor's commitment to a model).

Changing a subscription updates it in place as long as the Contributor has not signed their contract (or no contract exists); once it is signed, the change creates a new version and the future uninvoiced contributions of the previous version are replaced.
Defines the values of the variables of future contributions.
Rate applied to the amount excl. VAT to calculate the VAT and the amount incl. VAT of contributions and invoices.
Nature of the operation, a mandatory mention on the invoice.
Each of the successive states of a subscription within its subscription group.

A new version is created when you change a subscription whose contract has already been signed by the contributor; it replaces the future uninvoiced contributions of the previous version and gives rise to an amendment.
The version history can be viewed from the subscription page; only the latest version can be edited.
